methodological_rigor.justification: Rigorous preclinical study employing two syngeneic immune-competent mouse schwannoma models (cerebellopontine angle intracranial model using Gaussia luciferase reporter tracking; sciatic nerve peripheral model). Both sexes (1:1 ratio, ages 8-12 weeks) used to assess sex-related differences. Clearly defined endpoints (neurological symptoms for CPA, ~1 cm diameter for SN models). Treatment protocols specified with dosing/schedules (αPD1 200μg i.p. every 3 days; αVEGF 2.5mg/kg i.p. weekly). Flow cytometry with comprehensive immune cell panels (CD45, CD4, CD8, NK1.1, Gr1, CD11b, Granzyme B, perforin). Single-cell RNA-seq on human VS tissues from NF2-SWN patients (IRB-approved).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical study (LoE: 5) investigating immune checkpoint inhibition in NF2-related schwannomatosis, a rare hereditary tumor syndrome affecting 1/61,000 individuals. First comprehensive investigation of αPD1 efficacy in vestibular schwannomas. Mechanistic finding: αVEGF normalizes vasculature, enhancing αPD1 delivery and NK cell infiltration via NKG2D upregulation. Clinical relevance moderate: identifies potential combination strategy for patients with bevacizumab resistance/intolerance, but proof-of-concept limited to murine models. No patient efficacy data; translational path requires clinical validation.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive preclinical reporting: animal ethics compliance detailed; experimental design clearly specified (model selection rationale, cell lines, dosing); methods cover histology, FACS, audiometric testing (auditory brainstem responses), scRNA-seq (Cellranger v5.0.1, Seurat analysis documented). Human subject protocols (IRB approvals from Ohio State, MGH) disclosed. Western blot, ELISA, in vitro cytotoxicity assays all described. Limitations acknowledged (single cell models, limited human sample numbers for scRNA-seq). Supplementary Table 1 references supplementary data for antibody details.

novelty_literature.justification: Novel contribution: first comprehensive investigation of anti-PD1 monotherapy for schwannomas and hearing preservation outcomes. Combination mechanism elucidated: αVEGF-induced vessel normalization enhances αPD1 delivery and immune infiltration, promoting NKG2D-mediated NK/CD8 T cell cytotoxicity. However, PD-1 expression in VS previously reported; study confirms and extends known biology. Finding that αPD1+αVEGF outperforms monotherapies is incremental given similar combinations studied in other cancers. Addresses unmet need in NF2-SWN but limited mechanistic novelty beyond vascular normalization paradigm.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized preclinical study with clear rationale, two complementary animal models, and human tissue validation. Methods exceptionally detailed enabling reproducibility. Results systematically presented: tumor growth kinetics, immune profiling (flow cytometry), hearing function (ABRs), human scRNA-seq integration. Figures effectively demonstrate dose-response, immune cell kinetics, cytotoxicity data. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings within checkpoint inhibitor biology and unmet NF2-SWN treatment needs. Minor: methods section very dense but appropriately comprehensive.

key_strengths: Novel preclinical investigation: first comprehensive study of anti-PD1 efficacy in vestibular schwannomas and hearing preservation; identifies mechanism of αVEGF-induced vascular normalization enhancing αPD1 delivery and NKG2D-mediated immune cytotoxicity

Rigorous experimental design: two complementary in vivo models (intracranial CPA with Gluc reporter tracking; peripheral sciatic nerve) enabling evaluation of distinct microenvironments; balanced sex ratios assessing potential sex-related differences

Clinically relevant finding: combination therapy controls tumor growth resistant to αVEGF monotherapy, providing rationale for patients with bevacizumab intolerance/resistance in rare NF2-SWN population (1/61,000 incidence)

Human tissue validation: scRNA-seq on patient vestibular schwannomas from NF2-SWN patients (IRB-approved) confirms immune cell expression patterns and validates mechanistic findings from murine models
key_concerns: Limited clinical translation: preclinical only (LoE 5); no patient efficacy data or clinical trial results; αPD1 and αVEGF combination untested in humans with schwannomas; path to clinical development unclear
Small human sample size: scRNA-seq performed on human VS tissues but specific n for single-cell analysis not clearly stated; findings require validation in larger patient cohorts

Murine model limitations: genetically engineered Nf2−/− and SC4 cell lines may not fully recapitulate human vestibular schwannoma heterogeneity; immune microenvironment differences between murine subcutaneous/intracranial models and human tumors
Incomplete mechanistic characterization: identifies NKG2D upregulation as key but does not fully define upstream signaling pathways or identify therapeutic biomarkers predictive of response
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 3 paper: rigorous preclinical study with clear mechanistic insights and clinical relevance to rare NF2-SWN population. Combination strategy (αPD1+αVEGF) well-justified for patients with bevacizumab resistance. Limited clinical validation precludes higher tier. Recommend minor revisions regarding human sample characterization and clinical development pathway.
